bullets.title: ORCL: OCI accelerates to 121% y/y; GPU contracts renewing at 20% premium
bullets.body: Oracle Q1 revenue $19.35B beat consensus $19.14B; EPS $1.92 ex-items vs $1.74 expected. OCI growth accelerated to +121% y/y with backlog breadth widening; older-gen GPU contracts renewed at avg 20% premium. Q2 guide +30-34% cc, FY guide $90B+ maintained with $90-95B capex held; stock initially +7.6% pre-market but gave back gains intraday. Analyst tone broadly constructive; key bear is FCF inflection 1-2 years away as capex peaks.

bullets.title: ADBE: NNARR collapses 39% y/y; Hedgeye top short, Street mixed with 30% buy / 60% hold
bullets.body: Q3 revenue $6.76B beat slightly, EPS $6.13 vs $6.08 est, but net new ARR plunged to $400M (-39% y/y) and RPO growth decelerated to 8% y/y (first sub-10% since Q4 FY22). Q4 requires a 1.94x Q3-to-Q4 ARR step-up vs historical 1.39-1.41x norm. Citi cut PT to $250 (neutral), Wells raised to $270 (overweight), BMO raised to $270 (market perform); Hedgeye maintains top short citing organic ARR crossing into single-digit growth and incremental op margin collapsing to 26%.

bullets.title: RH: Q2 massive margin beat; MS Overweight $210 PT; 4Q guide of +16-21% sets high bar
bullets.body: RH Q2 gross margin 48.2% vs Street 43.3%; adj. EBITDA margin 19.4% vs 12.8% expected. Guides Q3 +5-6% and Q4 +16.1-21.2% revenue growth, with RH Estates contributing +8pts in Q4 and expected to be margin accretive representing 50% of offering within 5 years. MS maintains Overweight at $210 PT (47% upside, bull/bear $400/$50); some investors sidelined until sustainable demand proven; ~$50M tariff refund boosted results but ex-item gross margins contracted ~370bps.

bullets.title: MSFT: Plans to triple data center capacity to 38GW by 2032; bullish read-through for semis/DLR
bullets.body: Microsoft disclosed plans to expand data center capacity from ~12GW today to >38GW by 2032, adding ~4-4.5GW annually with ~1/3 AI GPUs and ~2/3 general CPU compute. Capacity shortage has already caused customers to migrate workloads elsewhere. Positive read-through for DLR (largest MSFT customer), AMD/INTC CPU demand, and CoWoS packaging supply chain per MS TMT.

bullets.title: SHOP: Bernstein initiates Outperform; Mizuho says Meta Muse concerns overblown
bullets.body: Bernstein initiated SHOP at Outperform citing AI headwinds offset by reduced entry barriers for merchants; stock +3.2-3.5% pre-market. Separately, Mizuho (Outperform) argues Meta Muse does not bypass Shopify Payments—virtual card transactions process normally with no economic change—and views agentic commerce as a new distribution channel rather than disintermediation risk. Shopify Catalog products convert 2x better than web-scraped results in LLM shopping; management expects flat headcount with AI driving operating leverage.

bullets.title: PLTR: DA Davidson raises PT to $250 on AI sovereignty positioning post-AIPCon11
bullets.body: DA Davidson upgraded PLTR to Buy and raised PT from $200 to $250, citing increased institutional investor interest following AIPCon11 focused on AI sovereignty. PLTR built a supply management system for NVIDIA leveraging Nemotron to address critical supply chain challenges; analyst sees long runway in data management, security, governance, and enterprise optimization beyond the core AI trade.

bullets.title: NVDA: CEO reaffirms 70% revenue growth for 2027; GPU demand signals corroborated by ORCL renewal premiums
bullets.body: NVIDIA CEO publicly reaffirmed 70% revenue growth forecast for 2027, citing deep reach across AI labs and cloud providers. ORCL's disclosure that mature NVDA GPUs (up to 4 years old) are being renewed at ~20% premiums corroborates sustained demand; Oppenheimer also initiated AEHR at Outperform/$120 PT flagging potential NVDA adoption of FOX-XP burn-in platform as a game-changing upside scenario ($6+ EPS vs $1.30 base).

bullets.title: TSLA: MS raises autonomous trucking bull case PT to $840; TAM $0.5-1.1tn by 2041
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its TSLA bull case PT to $840 (from $821) on autonomous trucking, modeling a $0.5-1.1tn US TAM by 2041 with ~20% lower cost per mile vs human drivers and ~7.5x profitability uplift. Serial AV trucking production expected to start 2027; technology and regulation seen as largely de-risked with OEM supply, lane coverage, and liability as key remaining risks.

bullets.title: SWKS: +9.1% on Goldman Sachs Communacopia conference commentary; options volume 692% above avg
bullets.body: Skyworks surged 9.1% with options volume spiking 692% above average (14,272 contracts vs 2,061 avg, P/C ratio 0.42) following commentary at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference. No specific financial disclosures noted but the move was the largest in the unusual options activity screen.

bullets.title: CRWV/SPCX: Neocloud pricing power validated; each $1M/MW/year above consensus worth $17/share to CRWV
bullets.body: 22V Research notes ORCL's 20% GPU renewal premiums validate neocloud pricing power. CRWV consensus implies ~$12M/MW/year but 22V sees $15-20M/MW realizable on 5.5GW open portfolio; each $1M/MW/year improvement = $17/share. SPCX disclosed a new $13B ARR compute deal starting December, boosting confidence in $100B ARR target; IREN validated $25M/MW/year pricing for 3-year deals and $40M/MW/year sub-1-year.

bullets.title: ADBE vs ORCL SaaS multiples: IGV -0.7% YTD; All-SaaS at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales, down 4.9% WoW
bullets.body: Wolfe Research SaaS daily notes IGV down 0.7% YTD vs S&P 500 +13.6%; All-SaaS index at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales (-4.9% WoW); All-Security at 8.2x (-4.5% WoW); All-Vertical at 5.9x (-7.5% WoW). ORCL and ADBE earnings are the dominant single-stock catalysts driving sector sentiment this morning.

bullets.title: TSLA/GOOGL: Fortum Google PPA priced at €80/MWh (+60% premium); MS raises Fortum PT to €25
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes the Fortum-Google power purchase agreement priced at ~€80/MWh, a 60% premium to forward power prices, and raised Fortum PT to €25. MS also highlights TSLA autonomous trucking and MSFT data center capex as key energy/clean-tech demand drivers; SEDG PT cut to $33 from $35 on near-term solar headwinds and conservative SST ramp.

bullets.title: SMR: UBS downgrades to Sell; 5Y+ timeline, no firm customer commitments vs. peers in construction
bullets.body: UBS downgraded NuScale Power (SMR) to Sell from Neutral, citing competitors already moving toward construction while SMR faces a 5-year-plus timeline to deployment and lacks firm customer commitments. Stock -4.1% pre-market.

bullets.title: DLR/VRT/CEG/VST: Roth Capital surveying political resistance to AI data-center power demand
bullets.body: Roth Capital plans a 1,000-1,250 person survey in high data-center-density regions (PJM, ERCOT) to quantify consumer blame attribution for rising electricity bills and assess emerging political-risk overlay on approval timelines. Focus names include power generators CEG, VST, TLN, GEV, VRT and data center operators EQIX, IREN, WULF, DLR. Ohio already canceled a $1.5B data-center tax exemption; Core Scientific received ERCOT approval for 1GW+ of Texas data centers.

bullets.title: CDNS: FBN Securities initiates Outperform at $375 PT, 30% upside
bullets.body: FBN Securities (Shelby Seyrafi) initiated Cadence Design Systems at Outperform with a $375 price target, implying ~30% upside from $288; FactSet consensus stands at $407.92. No specific thesis detail beyond the initiation was provided.

bullets.title: DELL: RBC initiates Outperform with $640 PT on AI server momentum
bullets.body: RBC Capital Markets initiated Dell Technologies at Outperform with a $640 price target, per the Wedbush/RBC morning sweep. The initiation is consistent with the broader AI infrastructure capex upcycle narrative given MSFT's 38GW data center expansion plan.

bullets.title: AVGO: Wolfe semiconductor webcast (9/15) to discuss AVGO earnings and QCOM-AMZN deal
bullets.body: Wolfe Research's 'Chips with Caso' webcast on September 15 at 10am ET will cover AVGO earnings takeaways and the QCOM-Amazon deal alongside Fall TMT Conference highlights. No directional view disclosed ahead of event.

bullets.title: August CPI: Core +0.29% MoM hawkish surprise; markets price 88-92% probability of September Fed hike
bullets.body: August core CPI came in at 0.29% MoM (consensus 0.20%), the second-hottest core services ex-housing print of the year, driven by lodging (+2.36%), airlines (+2.68%), education & communication (+1.85%), and shelter re-accelerating to 0.3% after 0.1% in July. Markets now pricing 88-92% probability of a September FOMC rate hike; Wolfe expects hikes in both September and December. Core PCE tracking ~22-25bp for August, suggesting disinflation at that level remains intact, but Fed credibility risk dominates the reaction function.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure capex cycle: OpenAI pausing Astra Pro subs on capacity constraints; compute scarcity persists
bullets.body: OpenAI suspended new $200/month ChatGPT Pro subscriptions due to unprecedented demand for its Astra model, validating sustained tight compute markets. MSFT's 38GW buildout, ORCL's accelerating OCI, and SPCX's new $13B ARR deal collectively point to a multi-year AI infrastructure super-cycle; 22V notes ~5% on the 10-year is the demand-destruction threshold and that AI buildout names should outperform as broader economy slows.

bullets.title: BBWI: Barington Capital builds 0.38% stake, pushing for sale, buybacks, board seats
bullets.body: Barington Capital disclosed a ~0.38% stake in Bath & Body Works, explicitly pushing for the company to explore a sale, accelerate buybacks, add board seats, and retain M&A advisers. Barington has prior activist wins at L Brands and Victoria's Secret; shares responded positively pre-market.
